translations.text: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, to fulfill the LORD’s word spoken by Jeremiah the prophet, the LORD stirred the spirit of the king of Persia. He issued a proclamation throughout his kingdom and also put it in writing, saying:
“This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me the kingdoms of the earth, and he has commissioned me to build him a house in Jerusalem, the city in Judah.
Whoever among you belongs to his people—may his God be with him—let him go up to Jerusalem in Judah and build the house of the LORD, the God of Israel. He is the God who is in Jerusalem.

As for anyone who remains in any place where he has been living as a foreigner, let the people of that place support him with silver, gold, possessions, and livestock, along with an offering for the house of God in Jerusalem.”
Then the heads of the ancestral families of Judah and Benjamin, the priests and Levites, and everyone whose spirit God had stirred arose to go up and build the house of the LORD God in Jerusalem.
All their neighbors supported them with articles of silver and gold, possessions, livestock, and valuable gifts, in addition to what they offered willingly.
King Cyrus brought out the articles belonging to the LORD’s house that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken from Jerusalem and placed in the house of his god.
Cyrus king of Persia brought them out through Mithredath the treasurer and handed them over to Sheshbazzar, the leader of Judah.
These were their numbers: thirty gold basins, one thousand silver basins, and twenty-nine robes;
There were 410 double silver bowls, also 30 gold bowls, and 1,000 other articles.
The gold and silver articles totaled 5,400. Sheshbazzar brought all of them up when the exiles came up from Babylon to Jerusalem.

These are the people of the province who came up from the captivity into which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken them, carrying them away to Babylon. They returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each going to his own town.
They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, and Baanah. The number of the men of Israel:
The descendants of Parosh: 2,172.
The descendants of Shephatiah: 372.
The descendants of Arah: 775.
The descendants of Pahath-moab, the descendants of Jeshua and Joab: 2,812.
The descendants of Elam: 1,254.
The descendants of Nethaniah: 945.
The descendants of Zaccai: 760.
The descendants of Bani: 142.
The descendants of Bebai: 623.
The descendants of Gaddar: 1,222.
The descendants of Arnakum: 666.
The descendants of Bigvai: 2,056.
The descendants of Adin: 464.
The descendants of Ater, of the family of Hezekiah: 98.
The descendants of Bezai: 323.
The descendants of Judah: 112.
The descendants of Hashum: 223.
The descendants of Gad: 95.
The people of Bethlehem: 123.
The men of Netophah: 56.
The men of Anathoth: 128.
The people of Azmaveth: 42.
The people of Kiriath-nearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth: 743.
The people of Ramah and Geba: 721.
The men of Michmash: 122.
The men of Bethel and Geder: 223.
The people of Nebo: 52.
The descendants of Magnash: 156.
The descendants of Elam: 1,254.
The descendants of Harim: 320.
The descendants of Lod, Hadir, and Ono: seven hundred and twenty-five.
The descendants of Jericho: three hundred and forty-five.
The people of Senaah: 3,630.
The priests: the descendants of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua: 773.
The descendants of Immer: 1,252.
The descendants of Pashhur: one thousand two hundred and seventy-four.
The descendants of Hadum: 1,017.
The Levites: the descendants of Jeshua and Kadmiah, and the descendants of Hodiah: 74.
Those who minister, the descendants of Asaph: one hundred and twenty-eight.

The descendants of Teral, the descendants of Shallum, the descendants of Ater, the descendants of Atalmon, the descendants of Jacob, the descendants of Hatita, and the descendants of Shobai: 139 in all.
The temple servants: the descendants of Neziah, the descendants of Hashuba, the descendants of Tabbaoth,
the descendants of Keros, the descendants of Siaha, the descendants of Paron.
The descendants of Lebaiah, the descendants of Hagabah, the descendants of Jacob.
The descendants of Hagab, the descendants of Shalmai, the descendants of Hanan.
The descendants of Gazel, the descendants of Hagar, the descendants of Dana.
The descendants of Dizon, the descendants of Dekora, the descendants of Gazzam.
The descendants of Uzza, the descendants of Pethah, the descendants of Besar.
The descendants of Asia, the descendants of Methanin, the descendants of Jephusin.
The descendants of Bakbuk, the descendants of Hakupha, the descendants of Hadhur.
The descendants of Bazlawaith, the descendants of Mehida, the descendants of Harsha.
The descendants of Karkos, the descendants of Sisera, the descendants of Timna.
The descendants of Neziah, the descendants of Hatupha.
The descendants of Eber, the descendants of Shallim, the descendants of Satim, the descendants of Aspheroth, the descendants of Peruda.
The descendants of Jaala, the descendants of Tarkon, the descendants of Giddel.
The descendants of Shephatiah, the descendants of Hattil, the descendants of Kebrath, the descendants of Hailtha, the descendants of Immer.
All the temple servants and the descendants of Eber and Shallim numbered 392.
These are those who came up from Tel-melah to Tel-abba and to Cherub; then it was said [?]. They could not establish their ancestral families or their descent, whether they were from Israel.
The descendants of Delaiah, the descendants of Tobiah, and the descendants of Nekariah numbered 652.

Among the descendants of the priests were the descendants of Habaiah, the descendants of Hakkoz, and the descendants of Barzillai, who had married one of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and had been called by their name.
These men searched in their genealogical register but could not find their records, and they were excluded from the priesthood.
The leaders of Israel told them not to eat any of the most holy offerings until a high priest arose who could inquire and discern.
The whole assembly together numbered 42,360,
Besides their male and female slaves, who numbered 7,337, they had 200 attendants who served them.
Their horses numbered 736, and their mules 245.
Their camels numbered 435, and their donkeys 6,720.
Some of the heads of ancestral families, when they entered the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, resolved to support the house of the Lord and rose to act.
According to their ability, they gave to the treasury for the work 61,000 gold darics, 5,000 minas of silver, and 100 tunics for the priests.

The priests, the Levites, some of the people, the attendants, the gatekeepers, the Nethinim, and those who had been assigned to service returned to their towns, and all Israel returned to their towns.
When the seventh month arrived, the Israelites were in their towns, and the people gathered as one in Jerusalem.

Jeshua son of Jozadak and his fellow priests, together with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his brothers, arose and built the altar of the God of Israel to offer burnt offerings on it, as written in the law of Moses, the prophet of God.

They set the altar in its place, because they were greatly afraid of the peoples living in the surrounding provinces. They offered burnt offerings on it to the LORD, burnt offerings morning and evening.
They celebrated the Festival of Shelters as prescribed in writing, offering the required number of burnt offerings each day according to the law, the amount appointed for each day.

Afterward they offered the regular burnt offering, the offerings for the new moon and all the LORD’s consecrated festivals, and the offerings of everyone who wished to make a voluntary offering to the LORD.
From the first day of the seventh month they began offering burnt offerings to the LORD, but the LORD’s temple had not yet been completed.

They gave money to the stonemasons and carpenters, and food, drink, and oil to the Tyrians and Sidonians to bring cedar timber from Lebanon by sea to Joppa, as Cyrus king of Persia had authorized them in writing.

In the second year after they came to the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Jeshua son of Jozadak, the rest of their brothers, the priests and Levites, and everyone who had come from captivity to Jerusalem gave orders. They appointed Levites twenty years old and older to supervise the work on the house of the Lord.

Jeshua, his brothers and sons, Kadmiel and his sons, and the sons of Hodaviah stood together to carry out the work on the house of the Lord, along with the sons of Henadad, their sons, and their brothers the Levites.

They laid the foundation for the building of the Lord’s temple. The priests stood dressed in their vestments, holding rams’ horns and blowing them, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, stood with trumpets to praise the Lord according to the directions of David king of Israel.

They blessed the Lord with thanksgiving and praise, because he is good and his kindness toward Israel lasts forever. All the people raised a great shout of praise to the Lord over the completion of the house of the Lord.

Many of the priests, Levites, and elderly heads of ancestral families who had seen this house in its former glory wept aloud when this house was completed. Many others raised their voices with horns and rejoicing.
None of the people could hear the sound of the horns because of the people’s loud weeping. The people were blowing the horns loudly, and the sound of weeping could be heard far away.
The enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the returned exiles were building a temple for the Lord, the God of Israel.

They approached Zerubbabel and the heads of the ancestral families and said to them, “Let us build with you too, because, like you, we will build for your God. We have been sacrificing to him here since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us up here.”

Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the rest of the heads of Israel’s ancestral families said to them, “You have no part with us in building a house for our God. We ourselves will build a house for the Lord, the God of Israel, as Cyrus king of Persia commanded us.”
The peoples of the land kept discouraging the people of Judah and frightening them so that they would not build.
They hired advisers against them to frustrate their plans throughout the days of Cyrus king of Persia, until the reign of Darius king of Persia.
During the reign of King Ahasuerus, at the beginning of his reign, an accusation was written against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.

In the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of their associates wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia, asking after his welfare. The letter was written in Aramaic and translated into Aramaic.
Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe wrote this letter concerning Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes, according to the prescribed form.
Then Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their associates—the judges, scribes, Tarpelites, Apharsites, Erechites, Babylonians, Susians, Dehavites, and Elamites—
and the rest of the nations whom the great and honored Osnappar had taken captive and settled in the towns of Samaria and the rest of the region Beyond the River, and so forth.
This is a copy of the letter they sent to King Artaxerxes: “Your servants, the people of Beyond the River, and so forth.

“Let it be known to the king that the Jews who came up from you to us have arrived in Jerusalem. They are rebuilding that rebellious and wicked city. They have completed its walls and joined its foundations together.
“Now let the king know that if that city is rebuilt and its walls are completed, you will receive no tribute, and they will pay you no tax. It will also undermine our plans.
“Now, because we eat the salt of the palace, it is not right for us to see the king dishonored. For this reason we have sent this message to inform you,

“so that you may read the record book of your ancestors. You will find in the record book and learn that this city is a rebellious city, harmful to kings and provinces, and that great conflicts have taken place within it since ancient times. That is why this city was destroyed.
“We inform the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are raised, you will consequently have no authority in Beyond the River.”
The king sent a reply to Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, the rest of their associates living in Samaria, and the rest of those living in Beyond the River: “Peace, and so forth.
The letter you sent me has been read accurately before me.
“I issued a decree, and they read and found that this city has risen against kings since ancient times, and that rebellion and great conflict have taken place within it.
“Mighty kings ruled over Jerusalem and governed all of Beyond the River, and they considered the former kings of no account.
“Now issue an order to stop those men, and do not let that city be rebuilt until I issue a command.”
Be watchful concerning this matter, so that the conflict does not increase and cause harm to the king.”

Then, when the copy of King Artaxerxes’ letter arrived, they read it before Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, and their associates. They then hurried to the Jews in Jerusalem and stopped them by overwhelming force.
Then work on the house of God in Jerusalem stopped, and it remained suspended until the second year of the reign of Darius, king of Persia.
Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo, the prophet, prophesied to the Jews in Jerusalem and Judah in the name of the God of Israel, who was over them.
Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak arose and began building the house of God in Jerusalem. The prophets of God were with them, helping them.
At that time Tattenai, governor of the region beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates came to them and said to the others, “Who commanded you to build this house and erect this wall?”
Then, in accordance with the law, they said to them, “What are the names of these men who are constructing this building?”
But God's eye was upon the exiles of Judah, and they did not stop until a report could go to Darius and a reply concerning this could then be returned.
A copy of the letter that Tattenai, governor of the region beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and his associates beyond the River sent to King Darius.
They sent him a report, and this was written in it: “To King Darius: Peace.

Let the king know that we went to Judah, the city of the great God. It is being built with large stones, and many beams are fastened into its walls. Great works are being carried out there, and the great undertaking is progressing toward completion in their hands.
Then we questioned those elders and said to them, “Who commanded you to build this house and erect this wall?”
We also asked them their names so that we could inform you by writing down the names of the men who lead them.

They gave us this answer: “We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth. The structure of this house that we are building was built many years ago, and the kings of Israel and their nobles completed it.
But because our ancestors angered the God of heaven, he handed them over to Nebuchadnezzar, the Chaldean king. He demolished this house and took the people captive to Babylon.
However, in the first year of Cyrus, king of Persia, King Cyrus issued a decree to rebuild this house of God.

King Cyrus also brought out of the temple in Babylon the gold and silver vessels of the house of God, which King Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem and carried to his temple in Babylon. He gave them to a man named Sheshbazzar, whom he had appointed governor.
He said to him, ‘Take these vessels. Go, carry them away, and place them in the temple in Jerusalem, and let that house itself be rebuilt on its site.’
Then this Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of the house in Jerusalem. From then until now it has been under construction and has not been finished.”

Now, if it pleases the king, let a search be made in the documents in the king's treasury in Babylon to determine whether King Cyrus did indeed command that this house of God in Jerusalem be built. Let the king send us his decision concerning this.
Then King Darius gave an order and read the records kept in the treasury there in Babylon.
He found a scroll in Ecbatana, a city in the province of Media, and this was written in it: “[?]

In the first year of King Cyrus, King Cyrus issued a decree and commanded that the house of God in Jerusalem be built as a place where sacrifices are offered, and that its foundations be raised. Its height was to be sixty cubits and its width twenty cubits.
Three courses of stone and new wooden doors; the expenses are to be paid from the royal treasury.

Also, the gold and silver vessels of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem and carried to Babylon, were handed over and returned to their place in the temple in Jerusalem, to their own location, and were stored in the house of God.
Now, Tattenai, governor of the region beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and his associates, the officials beyond the River, keep away from there.
Leave the work on the house of God to the Jews, so that they may carry it out, and leave the Jewish exiles alone, so that the house of God may be built on its site.

I have issued a decree concerning what you are to do [?] with those Jewish exiles to build that house of God: the expenses are to be paid and given to these men from the king's resources and the tribute of the region beyond the River, so that they do not stop the work.

Give them whatever they want, and let them lack nothing: young bulls, rams, and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, wheat, salt, wine, and oil. As the priests in Jerusalem direct, these are to be brought to them day by day, without neglect.
They are to offer sacrifices to the God of heaven and pray for the king and his sons.

I have also issued a decree that if anyone alters this order, a beam is to be pulled from his house and made into a cross for him, and he is to be crucified on it. His house is to be given over to plunder because of this.

And may God, whose name we found there, dwell there [?]. As for every king and people who stretches out a hand to alter or destroy this house of God in Jerusalem, I, Darius, have issued a decree that he perish quickly.
Then Tattenai, governor of the region beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and his associates promptly carried out what he had sent, in accordance with the decree.

The Jewish exiles worked and brought the undertaking toward completion through the prophecy of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo. They built and completed it according to the decree of the God of Israel and the decrees of Cyrus and Darius and the decree of Artaxerxes, king of Persia.
This house was completed on the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of King Darius.
The Israelites—the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the people of Judah—joyfully held a festival for this house, this house of God.

For the festival of the house of God they offered a hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and twelve male goats for the forgiveness of Israel’s sins, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
They appointed the priests to their duties and the Levites to their duties in the work of the house of God in Jerusalem, as it is written in the book of the law of Moses.
The returned exiles celebrated the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.

For the priests and Levites had purified themselves together, and all of them were purified. They slaughtered the Passover lambs for all those who had been in captivity, for their fellow priests, and also for themselves.
The Israelites who had come up from captivity in Babylon ate, as did everyone who had separated themselves from the impurity of the peoples of the land to pray before the Lord, the God of Israel.

They celebrated the Festival of Unleavened Bread joyfully for seven days, because the Lord had made them rejoice and had turned the hearts of the kings of Assyria toward them, to strengthen their hands in the work on the house of the Lord, the God of Israel.
After all these things, during the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Ezra son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah.
son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub,
son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth,
son of Zerahiah, son of Addi, son of Bukki,
son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest.

Ezra, who came up from Babylon, was a leader. He was a scribe skilled in the law of Moses, which the Lord, the God of Israel, had given him. The king granted him permission to follow the law of the Lord as he wished.

Some of the Israelites, some of the priests and Levites who served, some of the gatekeepers and temple servants, and some of those who went up to Jerusalem went up in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes.
They came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, in the seventh year of the king.
For they began to go up from Babylon in the first month, and on the first day of the fifth month they arrived in Jerusalem, with the favorable hand of God upon them.
For Ezra had prepared his heart to carry out the law of the Lord, to practice it, and to teach laws and judgments in Israel.
This is a copy of the letter that King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest, the scribe of the words and commandments of the Lord and his laws for all Israel.
King Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, the scribe learned in the law of the God of heaven: Greetings.
I have commanded and issued a decree that anyone in my kingdom from the people of Israel, the priests, or the Levites who wishes to go with you may go.
I have commanded and issued a decree, and I have sent some of those close to me to inquire about Judah and Jerusalem, and also to inquire about the law of your God, which is in your hands.
You are to carry the king’s silver and gold, which I have willingly offered to the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, that dwelling place.
All the silver and gold that you find throughout the province of Babylon shall go with you. The priests and Levites and those who wish to go with you shall go to the house of God in Jerusalem.
Now take care to buy with this money bulls, rams, and lambs, their offerings and their drink offerings, and offer them on the altar of your God in Jerusalem.
Whatever you and your brothers think good to do with the rest of this money, do according to the will of your God.
The vessels given to you for the service of the house of your God, deliver before God in Jerusalem.
Any additional vessels you need for the service of the house of your God, take from the king’s treasury and provide them.
I, King Artaxerxes, have issued a decree to all the treasurers beyond the River: whatever Ezra the priest, the scribe versed in the law of the God of heaven, asks of you, you must do diligently.
Up to a hundred talents of silver, up to a hundred kors of wheat, up to a hundred quarters of wine, up to a hundred quarters of oil, and salt without a prescribed limit.

Everything is to be supplied by written order. Give it to him according to the law of his God. Let him receive and carry out the law of the God of heaven, so that there will be no wrath against the kingdom of the king and his sons.
We also inform you that you have no authority to make any demand of any of the priests, Levites, horn blowers, or workers in the house of God.

And you, Ezra the scribe, according to the wisdom that your God has given you, appoint officials and judges to judge all the people beyond the River, all who know the law of your God. Teach anyone who does not know it.
Anyone who does not obey the law of your God and the law of the king must promptly have judgment carried out against him, whether for death or for life, for the loss of property, or for imprisonment.
Blessed are you, Lord, God of our ancestors, who put this intention into the king’s heart, to glorify the house of the Lord in Jerusalem.

He extended his kindness to me before the king and before all the king’s mighty officials. I was strengthened because the hand of the Lord my God was upon me, and I chose leading men from Israel to go up with me.
These are the names of the heads of their ancestral families who were registered by genealogy and came up with me from Babylon during the reign of King Artaxerxes.
From the descendants of Phinehas, Gershom; from the descendants of Tamar, Daniel; from the descendants of David, Hattush.
From the descendants of Shecaniah and from the descendants of Parosh, Zechariah, and with him 150 males were registered.
From the descendants of Pahath-moab: Elijah and Hanani son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred males.
From the descendants of Shecaniah, son of Jahaziel, and with him 300 males.
From the descendants of Azzun, Ebed son of Jonathan, and with him 50 males.
From the descendants of Elam, Jeshaiah son of Nethaniah, and with him 70 males.
From the descendants of Shebatiah, Zechariah son of Michael, and with him 80 males.
From the descendants of Joab, Obadiah son of Nahael, and with him 218 males.
From the descendants of Shelomith, son of Josiphiah, and with him 260 males.
From the descendants of Bebai: Zechariah son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight males.
Of the descendants of Azgad: Johanan son of Zechariah, and with him 110 males.
From the descendants of Arnakum, [?], whose names were Eliphelet, Neaiel, and Shemaiah, and with them sixty males.
From the descendants of Bigvai: Uthai and Zaccur, and with them sixty males.
I gathered them at the river that flows to Ahava, and we camped there for three days. I examined the people and the priests, but I found none of the descendants of Levi there.
I sent for Eleazar, Araniah, Shemaiah, Anathan, Jarib, Eliathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam, the leaders, and for Jonadab and Eliathan. All these were leaders.

I sent them with instructions to Iddo, their leader in the place called Casiphia. I put words in their mouths to speak with Haddi, our brother, who lived in Casiphia, to bring us servants for the house of our God.
Because the hand of our God was gracious toward us, they brought us a wise man from the descendants of Mahli, son of Levi, son of Israel, and Shereiah with his brothers and sons, twelve in all.
And Hashabiah, and with him Isaiah from the descendants of Merari, with his brothers and sons, twenty in all.
From the men whom David had given for the service of the Levites, the temple servants, there were two hundred and twenty. All of them were named individually.
At the river Ahava I proclaimed and instructed them to fast before our God and to ask him for a safe journey for us, our children, and all our possessions.

For I was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen to help protect us from our enemies on the journey, because we had told the king, “The hand of God is with everyone who seeks him, for their good, but his power and anger are against everyone who abandons him.”
So we fasted and petitioned our God about this, and he heard us.
I chose twelve of the senior priests: Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their brothers with them.
I counted out to them the silver, gold, and vessels, the offering for the house of our God that the king, his nobles, his officials, and all the Israelites present there had given.
I weighed out into their charge 150 talents of silver, a hundred silver utensils, and a hundred talents of gold.
There were twenty gold bowls, a thousand darics, and vessels of fine Corinthian bronze, as beautiful as gold.
I said to them, “You are holy, and the vessels are holy. The silver and gold are an offering to the Lord, the God of your ancestors.
Be watchful and guard them until you hand them over before the chief priests, the Levites, and the heads of Israel’s ancestral families in Jerusalem, in the temple of the house of the Lord.”
The priests and Levites accepted responsibility for delivering the silver, gold, and vessels by weight and bringing them to Jerusalem, to the house of our God.

We set out from the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month to go to Jerusalem. The hand of God was upon us, and he rescued us from the power of our enemies and from those lying in ambush along the road.
We came to Jerusalem and stayed there for three days.

On the fourth day we weighed the silver, gold, and vessels in the house of our God and handed them over to Meremoth son of Uriah the priest. With him was Eleazar son of Phinehas, and with them were the Levites Jehozabar son of Jeshua and Jodaiah son of Bigvai.
Everything was counted and weighed, and the total weight was recorded at that time.

Those who had come from captivity, the returned exiles, offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats for the forgiveness of sins. All these were burnt offerings to the Lord.
He delivered the king’s decree to the king’s officials and to the governors of the region beyond the River. They honored the people and the house of God.

When all these things were finished, the elders approached me and said, “The people of Israel, the priests, and the Levites have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands and their uncleanness: the Canaanites, Hittites, Ammonites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Egyptians, Moabites, and Amorites.

For they have taken some of their daughters as wives for themselves and their sons, and the holy offspring have become mixed with the peoples of the lands. The elders and the Levites have taken the lead in this wrongdoing.”
When I heard this, I tore my clothes and my cloak, pulled out some of the hair of my head and beard, and sat stunned.
Everyone who was concerned about the word of the God of Israel gathered around me because of the wrongdoing committed by the returned exiles. I sat stunned until the ninth hour.
At the ninth hour I rose from my grief and from tearing my clothes, knelt down, and spread out my hands in prayer before the Lord God.
I said, “My God, we are ashamed to lift our faces to you, our God, because our guilt has risen above our heads and our great sins have reached heaven.

From the days of our ancestors until today, we have been guilty of great sins. Because we, our ancestors, our kings, and our priests have sinned so greatly, we have been handed over to the sword, captivity, plunder, and public shame, into the hands of the kings of the lands and into the hands of our enemies, as we are today.

And now, for a very short time, may there be mercy from the Lord our God, to leave us a remnant and give us a place in his holy land, so that our God may brighten our eyes and give us a little life in our slavery.

For we are slaves, yet our God has not abandoned us in our slavery. Our God has granted us mercy before the king of Persia and has given us our daily provision, so that we may restore the house of our God, rebuild its ruins, and be given a protective wall in Judah and Jerusalem.
Now what can we say after all these things? For we have abandoned your commandments.

You commanded us through your servants the prophets and told us, “The land you are entering to possess is unclean through the uncleanness of the peoples and cities. In their uncleanness they have filled it from end to end; they have filled it with their hateful deeds.

So now, do not give your daughters to their sons, and do not take their daughters for your sons. Never seek their peace or prosperity, so that you may become strong, eat the good things of the land, and pass it on to your children, who will inherit it forever.”
And after all these things that have come upon us because of our evil deeds and our great sins, you, our God, resolved to forgive our sins and give us a remnant in the world.

Yet we turned back and broke your commandments. We went and joined ourselves to these unclean peoples and acted as they did. But you are merciful. Do not be angry with us. Forgive our offenses before you. Because you are merciful, leave us survivors in the world, for there is no one like you, so that we may not perish.
LORD, God of Israel, you are righteous, for you have left a remnant of us, as we are today. Here we stand, confessing our sins before you, for we have nothing to say before you about this.

While Ezra prayed and confessed, lying prostrate and weeping before the house of the LORD, a very large assembly of Israelites—men, women, and children—gathered around him, for the children were weeping very bitterly.

Then Shecaniah son of Nahiel, one of the descendants of Elam, spoke to Ezra the scribe: “We have been unfaithful to the LORD our God and have married foreign women from the peoples of the land. Yet even now there is hope for Israel concerning this.
Now let us swear oaths before our God to send away all the foreign women and those born to them. Act according to the counsel of the LORD and of those who fear the law of our God.”
Confirm it, for this decision rests with you. We are with you. Be strong and act.”
Then Ezra the scribe stood up and made the elders of the priests, the Levites, and all Israel swear to act according to this command, and they swore.

Then Ezra the scribe rose from before the house of the LORD and went to the chamber of Johanan son of Eliashib. He stayed there, eating no bread and drinking no water, because he was grieving over the people's wrongdoing.
Heralds proclaimed throughout Judah and Jerusalem that all those who had returned from captivity were to gather in the city of Jerusalem.

Anyone who did not come within three days would be dealt with according to the decision of the elders and officials: his possessions would be destroyed, and he himself would be excluded from the people of Israel.

All the men of Judah and Benjamin gathered in Jerusalem within three days, in the ninth month, on the tenth day of the month. All the LORD's people gathered in the square of the LORD's temple, shaking and trembling over the matter.
Ezra the priest stood up and said to them, “You have been unfaithful to God and have married foreign women, adding to Israel's sins.
Now make confession to the LORD, the God of your ancestors, and do his will. Separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from the foreign women.”
All the people answered Ezra in a loud voice: “What you have told us is right. Everything you tell us to do is accepted, and we will carry it out faithfully.
But now the people are many, and it is the rainy season. We cannot stand in the square, and this is not a task for one or two days, for our sins in this matter are many.

Now let our elders and all the people take their stand. Let all those in our villages who have married foreign women come at the time of prayer, together with the elders and judges of each village, until they turn away our God's burning anger from us concerning this oath.”
Jonathan son of Ammuel, Nehaziah son of Tekoa, and Meshullam took charge of this matter, and Mattai the Levite was their helper.

The returned exiles did so. Ezra selected priests, ten men who were heads of ancestral families, according to their ancestral houses. All of them were designated by name. They sat down on the first day of the tenth month to investigate the matter.
They finished dealing with all the men who had married foreign women by the first day of the first month.
Among the descendants of the priests, the following were found to have married foreign women: from the descendants of Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers, Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jonadab, and Gedaliah.
They too agreed to send away their wives, and they offered rams from the flock for their sins.
From the descendants of Immer: Hanani and Zechariah.
From the descendants of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.
From the descendants of Pashhur: Elin, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabar, and Elasiah.
From the Levites: Jozabar, Shimei, Kelna, Kelita, Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
From the attendants: Eliashib. From the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
From Israel, from the descendants of Parosh: Jeremiah, Jezaniah, Malchijah, Benjamin, Lazir, Malchijah, and Benaiah.
From the descendants of Elam: Nethaniah, Zechariah, Neaiel, Abri, Jeremoth, and Elihu.
From the descendants of Zattu: Elani, Eliashib, Nethaniah, Jeremoth, Zabbur, and Uzziah.
From the descendants of Bebai: Johanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai.
From the descendants of Bani: Baki from Tashlum, Malluch, Uzziah, Jashub, Saul, and Jeremoth.
From the descendants of Pahath-moab: Gedaliah, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, and his sons, the descendants of Manasseh.
The descendants of Harim: Eliezer, Malchijah, Anshua, Shemaiah, and Simeon.
Benjamin, Malluch, and Shemaiah.
Of the descendants of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zaccur, Eliphelet, Carmi, Manasseh, and Shimei.
From the descendants of Baki: Madrai, Amram, and Joel.
And Beziah son of Kelihu.
And Nehaiel, Meremoth, and Eliashib.
Mattaniah, Mattenai, and Uthai.
And Bani and his sons, Shimei.
And Shelemiah, Nathan, and Azariah.
And Machizab, Shashai, and Sharai.
And Adriel and Shemariah.
And Shallum, Amariah, and Joseph.
From the descendants of Nebo: Nebael, Mattithiah, Zaccur, Zebina, Joel, and Benaiah.
All these had married foreign women, and some of them had fathered children.
